title: MCP (Model Context Protocol): how agents reach tools, and where you can stop them
summary: The advanced connector policy API shown creates a policy but does not apply it to an environment or environment group. Microsoft documents assignment as a separate required operation, so following this row alone would leave the intended restriction unenforced. The other control paths and commands are supported; two documentation disagreements should also be noted.

claims.claim: Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Block restricts an MCP server and all its tools across the organisation.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools, and then select the Registry tab. ... Select Block to restrict the server across your organization

claims.claim: Individual tools are managed under Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Tools using Enabled or Disabled toggles and Save.
claims.quote: Select the Tools tab. The list shows every tool the server exposes, along with its description and an Enabled or Disabled toggle.

claims.claim: MCP server requests are reviewed at Agents > Tools > Requests (preview) in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools, and then select the Requests (preview) tab.
claims.fix: Keep this path, but note that https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/developer/reference/cli/develop-mcp instead points administrators to Requested Agents for pending requests. Cite that conflicting reference alongside the current admin procedure.

claims.claim: Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access governs availability by publisher type, including connectors and MCP servers.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access.

claims.claim: Agents > Settings > User access governs which users can access agents and plugins, including MCP servers and connectors.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Settings > User access to manage your organization's agents and plugins.

claims.claim: Federated connectors can be enabled or disabled in Copilot > Connectors > Your connections and staged with Staged rollout > Add staging.
claims.quote: Limit a connector to specific users or Microsoft Entra ID groups by choosing Add staging in the Staged rollout column.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP tenant policy is configured at Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Agents > Tools. ... In the tools registry, select Work IQ MCP. ... select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: Advanced connector policies for environment connector and MCP server governance are reached through Security > Data and privacy > Advanced connector policies.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select Security. ... In the Security pane, select Data and privacy. ... Select Advanced connector policies.

claims.claim: POST https://api.powerplatform.com/governance/ruleBasedPolicies?api-version=2024-10-01 is the automation equivalent for imposing the environment or environment-group connector allowlist.
claims.quote: Adding ACP to an environment group is a two-part operation: create the policy, then assign it to the group. The create call returns the new policy id, which you use in the assignment call.
claims.fix: Label the existing POST as creating an unassigned policy, not applying governance. Include its documented name/ruleSets body with ConnectorManagement, version and inputs.AllowedConnectorList, then POST https://api.powerplatform.com/governance/ruleBasedPolicies/<policyId>/environmentGroups/<environmentGroupId>/assignments?api-version=2024-10-01 with {} to apply it to a group. For a single environment, use /governance/ruleBasedPolicies/<policyId>/environments/<environmentId>/assignments?api-version=2024-10-01 with {}. The cited tutorial documents both assignment operations.

claims.claim: Classic data policies are created at Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: In the Security pane, under Settings, select Data and privacy. ... select the Data policy section. Select + New Policy.

claims.claim: New-DlpPolicy in Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell accepts DisplayName, EnvironmentType and optional Environments to create a data policy.
claims.quote:
New-DlpPolicy
    -DisplayName <String>
    -EnvironmentType <String>
    [-DefaultConnectorClassification <String>]
    [-Environments <Object>]

claims.claim: Dataverse MCP environment and client settings are under Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Dataverse Model Context Protocol > Advanced Settings.
claims.quote: Select Manage > Environments. ... select Settings. Under Settings, select Product > Features. Scroll down to locate Dataverse Model Context Protocol ... Select Advanced Settings.

claims.claim: PATCH /api/data/v9.2/allowedmcpclients(<allowedmcpclientid>) with isenabled false or true disables or enables an individual client.
claims.quote: Entity set path: ... [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/allowedmcpclients ... Primary key: ... allowedmcpclientid ... Operations supported: ... POSTGETPATCHDELETE ... isenabled | Edm.Boolean | Display name: Is Enabled

claims.quote: Resources: File-like data that an agent can read for more context, such as API responses or file contents

claims.quote: Tools: Functions that a language model can call to perform an action

claims.claim: Work IQ offers a remote MCP server.

claims.claim: Where a federated connector supplies the tools, Copilot can create, update or delete data on the user's behalf.
claims.quote: Where a connector provides the tools, Copilot can also create, update, or delete data in the connected system on the user's behalf.
claims.fix: Keep the qualified statement, but cite and note the inconsistent overview at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/overview#types-of-copilot-connectors, which still says federated connectors are read-only while also announcing write actions from early October 2026. Prefer the detailed current procedure without silently hiding the disagreement.

claims.claim: Advanced connector policies support MCP server-level blocking but not individual MCP tool control.
claims.quote: As of now, granular control over individual MCP tools (endpoints and actions) within an MCP server isn't available. Blocking the entire MCP server is supported.

claims.claim: Advanced connector policy allowlist enforcement starts on saving a single-environment policy or publishing an environment-group policy.

claims.quote: Blocking an MCP server also blocks dependent plugins and linked connectors.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio makes the customer responsible for tools and resources accessed from non-Microsoft MCP servers.

claims.claim: Data processed by non-Microsoft services is not subject to Microsoft agreements.
